module purpose: neorv32_pwm is a bus-accessed PWM peripheral that instantiates up to NUM_CHANNELS channel blocks; each generated channel stores a control word, can return that word on readback, and generates one PWM bit from the selected clock-generator input and internal counters. The top entity decodes per-channel read/write strobes, aggregates channel readback into the bus response, OR-reduces channel clock-generator requests to clkgen_en_o, and packs channel PWM bits into the 16-bit pwm_o vector.

use-case flows.value: per-channel bus access qualification for a read or write request
a selected channel's control register word: enable, prescaler select, polarity, clock-divider limit, and duty threshold
the selected channel's stored control register word returned through channel readback and the top-level bus response path
enabled channels request clock generation and update divider state, duty state, and PWM output from the stored control register
bus response, channel configuration, counters, and PWM output forced to zero or terminate values while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: Per-channel bus access qualification -- which generated channel a request addresses, and whether it is a write or a read
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start of both configure and read-out flows is the decoded access decision in the top entity: line 109 computes sel(i) from the address comparison, line 110 computes we(i) from sel(i), bus_req_i.stb and bus_req_i.rw, and line 111 computes re(i) from sel(i), bus_req_i.stb and not bus_req_i.rw. These decisions directly gate configuration writes in the channel at line 183 and readback at line 194 through the connections at lines 99-100. Integrity requires only the addressed channel to be written or read; availability is that the strobes are produced when those predicates hold. bus_req_i is a transport record, so the eligible structural references are the internal decisions sel, we and re.

conceptual assets.concept: Per-channel PWM control register -- enable, prescaler select, output polarity, clock-divider limit, and duty threshold
conceptual assets.reasoning: In each generated channel instance, line 183 enables a register update and lines 184-188 load cfg_en, cfg_prsc, cfg_pol, cfg_cdiv and cfg_duty from wdata_i. The stored values are returned on rdata_o at line 194 and drive operation at lines 197 and 214-234. Integrity requires these stored settings to match the written bits because they determine whether the channel runs, which clkgen_i bit is used, the divider terminal count, the duty compare threshold, and the output polarity; availability is that they persist between writes and reset to zero at lines 177-181.

conceptual assets.concept: Aggregate clock-generator enable request -- whether any generated channel currently requests clkgen activity
conceptual assets.reasoning: PWM operation depends on external clkgen_i pulses, and the top entity requests them with clkgen_en_o <= or_reduce_f(ce) at line 121. Each ce(i) is driven from a generated channel connection at line 104, where the channel copies cfg_en to its local clkgen_en_o at line 197. Integrity requires the consumer of clkgen_en_o to receive exactly that any-channel-enabled decision; availability is that the request is produced combinationally from the current channel requests.

conceptual assets.concept: Per-channel PWM timing state -- current divider count, divider tick event, and duty counter state
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate flow keeps live state for each generated channel: when cfg_en = '1' and the selected clkgen_i bit is high, lines 214-220 compare cnt_cdiv with cfg_cdiv, reset or increment cnt_cdiv, and assert cnt_tick at line 217; lines 224-227 clear or increment cnt_duty based on cfg_en and cnt_tick. These state values feed the output decision at line 231. Integrity requires this progression state to obey those update rules because corrupt state changes the timing and duty position of the PWM waveform; availability is that it advances under the RTL-visible conditions and clears on reset or disable (lines 203-206, 213, 225).

conceptual assets.concept: PWM output waveform -- the per-channel level delivered to the top-level pwm_o vector
conceptual assets.reasoning: Each channel computes its output at lines 231-234: if cfg_en = '0' or unsigned(cnt_duty) >= unsigned(cfg_duty) then pwm_o is driven with cfg_pol, else with not cfg_pol; reset forces '0' at line 207. The top entity clears the full vector at line 116 and copies the generated channel bits into pwm_o(pwm'range) at line 117. Integrity requires consumers to receive exactly this computed waveform; availability is per-edge update in the channel and delivery on the top-level output vector.
